14-002.r: Meghalaya plateau → extension of the Peninsular Plateau, separated from it by the Malda Gap.

14-003.r: Extra-peninsular mountains of India (e.g. Himalayan ranges) → formed in the Cenozoic era.

14-004.r: Dhanbad is the most densely peopled district of the Chotanagpur plateau because of mining industries and industrialisation (coal); its red soil is poor for farming.

14-005.r: Chota Nagpur Plateau (about 86239 sq km, mainly Jharkhand) → a front-sloping series of plateaus at different levels with steep scarps; Patland about 1100 m high.

14-006.r: Map: A → Narmada–Tapti rift valley; B → Chhattisgarh plain (Mahanadi); C → Chota Nagpur plateau; D → rain-shadow area of the Western Ghats.

14-007.r: Malwa Plateau → between the Aravalli (north) and Vindhya (south), Bundelkhand plateau to the east; about 150000 sq km, 530 km long, 390 km wide.

14-008.r: Southern part of the Vindhyan Scarpland → Bhander plateau (steep, rugged; part of the Vindhya Mountains).

14-009.r: Dandakaranya (about 89078 sq km) → Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh; about 480 km east–west and 320 km north–south.

14-011.r: Dandakaranya → central India, part of the Peninsular plateau, spread over Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.

14-012.r: Oldest part of Bihar → Kharagpur Hills (Dharwar); Rohtas plateau → Vindhyan; North-Western Hills → Tertiary; North Ganga plain → youngest.

14-013.r: Meghalaya Plateau → Garo, Khasi and Jaintia Hills; Bhuban Hills lie in the Barak Valley, Assam (not part of it).
14-013.h: West to east 'G-K-J': Garo, Khasi, Jaintia.

14-014.r: Albama Hill → south of the Bijapur upland.

14-015.r: Peninsular plateau → irregular triangle rising from 150 m to 600–900 m; edges: Delhi ridge (NW), Rajmahal hills (E), Gir range (W), Cardamom hills (S). Both correct.

14-016.r: Not true: plateau height 1000–1500 m (it is 600–900 m); Gir in the east, Rajmahal in the west (it is the reverse). True: height generally falls from west to east.

15-001.r: Statement I false: plate tectonics (1960s) grew from many scientists – Wilson, Morgan, Parker, McKenzie, Harry Hess. II true: it rests on sea-floor spreading theory.

15-002.r: India's mean sea level → measured with reference to the Chennai coast.

15-003.r: India's territorial waters → 12 nautical miles from the coast.

15-004.r: India's coastline → about 7500 km (7516.6 km; re-verified 2023: 11098.81 km); longest state coastline → Gujarat (1214.7 km; now 2340.62 km).

15-010.r: 'Ratnakara' (place of gems and jewels) → ancient Indian name for the Indian Ocean.

15-011.r: Most coastal erosion → by waves (tides, currents, tsunamis and human activity also erode).

16-001.r: West coast, north to south → Janjira (Raigad, Maharashtra), Sindhudurg (Maharashtra), Kannur (Kerala), Nagercoil (Kanyakumari district, Tamil Nadu).

16-002.r: Tharangambadi (Tamil Nadu coast) → Danish colony from 1620 to 1845; New Jerusalem and Zion churches; sold to the British in 1845.

16-003.r: Lines along India's coast on the map → underwater relief contours (sea-floor depth): continental coast, continental slope, deep-sea plains, ocean trenches.

16-004.r: West coast → Janjira (Raigad, Maharashtra) and Udupi (Karnataka). East coast → Auroville (Coromandel, Tamil Nadu–Puducherry) and Tuticorin (south-east Tamil Nadu).

16-005.r: Digha → West Bengal; Gopalpur → Odisha; Calangute → Goa; Marina → Tamil Nadu.

16-006.r: Coromandel Coast → coast of Tamil Nadu (and Andhra Pradesh), from the Krishna delta (False Divi Point) to Cape Comorin (Kanyakumari).

16-010.r: West coast: north → Konkan, south → Malabar. East coast: north → Northern Circars, south → Coromandel.
16-010.h: Each coast north to south: West K-M (Konkan, Malabar), East N-C (Northern Circars, Coromandel).

16-011.r: Rann of Kutch (Kachchh, Gujarat; and Sindh) → salt marsh, once a shallow arm of the Arabian Sea; best example of repeated sea-level falls creating marshland.

17-001.r: Saddle Peak (732 m) → highest peak of Andaman & Nicobar, near Diglipur on North Andaman.

17-003.r: Andaman and Nicobar → a group of islands (UT) between the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea.

17-004.r: Andaman and Nicobar → 836 islands, islets and rock outcrops; none of the options fits. The book gives no single answer (*).

17-005.r: Ten Degree Channel (along 10° N, about 150 km wide) → separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands.

17-008.r: Only statement 1 correct: Barren Island (Andaman Sea) is an active volcano in Indian territory; it lies about 135 km NE of Port Blair and about 540 km from Great Nicobar.

17-009.r: Barren Island → Andaman Sea, Bay of Bengal, about 135 km north-east of Port Blair; South Asia's only active volcano; first recorded eruption 1787.

17-010.r: Volcanic island of India → Barren Island (Andaman), the only confirmed active volcano in South Asia.

17-012.r: India's two volcanic islands → Barren (active) and Narcondam (dormant/inactive), both in the Andaman Sea.

17-013.r: Sriharikota island (Andhra Pradesh) → separates Pulicat Lake from the Bay of Bengal; site of the Satish Dhawan Space Centre.

17-014.r: Adam's Bridge (Ram Setu) → chain of shoals from Dhanushkodi on Pamban island to Mannar island (Sri Lanka); Pamban Bridge is 2.2 km long.

17-015.r: Closest to Great Nicobar (India's southernmost island, about 540 km from Port Blair) → Sumatra (Indonesia); Borneo, Java and Sri Lanka are farther.

18-001.r: Lakshadweep → 36 coral islands in the Arabian Sea; capital Kavaratti; largest Andrott; Minicoy (second largest) cut off by the 9° Channel.

18-002.r: Correct: Lakshadweep is made of small coral islands; earlier called Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi. Wrong: it lies near the Coromandel coast (it is near Kerala's Malabar coast).

18-003.r: Tilanchong → Andaman and Nicobar Islands, not Lakshadweep; Agathi, Kavaratti and Kalpeni → Lakshadweep (Laccadive).

18-004.r: Atolls in India → commonly found near Lakshadweep.

18-005.r: Coral island → Lakshadweep (Arabian Sea, south-west of India; capital Kavaratti).

18-008.r: Lakshadweep → built by coral-reef accumulation. Coral reefs in India: A&N, Gulf of Mannar, Lakshadweep, Malvan, Gulf of Kutch; not the Gulf of Cambay.

18-010.r: Remotest island from the Indian coast among options → Minicoy (Lakshadweep); Bhatkal, Arnala and Henry are offshore islands.

18-011.r: Island between India and Sri Lanka → Rameswaram (Ramanathapuram district, Tamil Nadu); Elephanta is near Mumbai; Nicobar lies in the south-east Bay of Bengal.

18-012.r: Large city built on an Indian island → Mumbai (largest island city as a township; Port Blair is larger only in area).

18-013.r: Most populous island of India → Salsette, on which Mumbai city and Thane district stand.

18-014.r: Viyant Syodhar → Gulf of Kutch; Piram → Gulf of Cambay (Khambhat); Dwarka → Arabian Sea coast; Diu → Kathiawar coast.

18-015.r: Divi (Diviseema) Island → among the distributaries of the Krishna, Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh; cyclone-prone delta.

18-016.r: Kori Creek → tidal creek in the Rann of Kutch (Gujarat), on the India–Pakistan maritime border.

18-017.r: Sir Creek → 96 km tidal estuary in the Rann of Kutch between Gujarat (India) and Sindh (Pakistan); India–Pakistan boundary dispute.

19-002.r: Vidarbha → eastern region of Maharashtra; two divisions: Nagpur and Amravati.

19-003.r: Pat region (high hill peaks) → Chota Nagpur region, mostly in Jharkhand.

19-004.r: Jhumri Telaiya (famous for radio song requests) → Koderma district, Jharkhand.

19-005.r: 'Kohinoor of India' → Andhra Pradesh; the Kohinoor diamond came from its Kollur mine.

19-006.r: Manipur → mostly mountainous: hills cover about 90% (20089 sq km) of its 22,327 sq km; valleys only about one-tenth.

19-007.r: Phumdi → floating mass of vegetation, soil and organic matter in Loktak lake, Manipur; home of the endangered Sangai deer.

19-008.r: 'Silicon State' → Karnataka; its capital Bengaluru is the 'Silicon Valley of India'.

19-010.r: Correct pair: Palanpur–Gujarat. Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar) → Maharashtra; Hubli → Karnataka; Guntur → Andhra Pradesh.

19-011.r: Wrong pair: Andhra Pradesh–Malnad; Malnad (dense forest) is in Karnataka. Correct: Chhattisgarh–Chhattisgarh plain; Jharkhand–Chota Nagpur; Maharashtra–rain-shadow region.

19-012.r: NCR → Delhi + Haryana sub-region (14 districts incl. Rohtak, Karnal) + UP sub-region (8 districts incl. Bulandshahr); Khurja, Karnal, Rohtak in; Ambala and Punjab out.

19-014.r: West to east → Bikaner (Rajasthan), Aligarh (UP), Darbhanga (Bihar), Nagaon (Assam).

19-015.r: J&K map: A → Baramula, B → Srinagar, C → Anantnag, D → Kargil.

19-016.r: MP now borders five states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, UP, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra (answer 'seven' dates from 1993). Bhopal lies south of the Tropic of Cancer; J&K touches Punjab.
19-016.c: Right when asked (1993): Madhya Pradesh then touched seven states. Since Chhattisgarh was carved out of it, it borders only five (Gujarat, Rajasthan, UP, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra), so (a) is wrong today.

19-017.r: Area (Census 2011), descending → MP 3,08,252 > UP 2,40,928 > Andhra Pradesh 1,60,205 > Bihar 94,163 sq km.

19-018.r: Smallest among the options → Tamil Nadu; Andhra Pradesh (after bifurcation) 160205, Karnataka 191,791, Gujarat 196244 sq km.

19-019.r: UP ranks 4th by area, after Rajasthan (342,239 sq km), MP (308,252) and Maharashtra (307,713). By population the top three are UP, Maharashtra, Bihar.

19-020.r: Maharashtra → 2nd in population and 3rd in area (Census 2011).

19-021.r: Three largest states (nearly 30% of India's 3287469 sq km) → Rajasthan (3,42,239), Madhya Pradesh (3,08,252), Maharashtra (3,07,713 sq km).
19-021.h: Big three by area 'R-M-M': Rajasthan, MP, Maharashtra.

19-023.r: Area descending → Chhattisgarh (135,192 sq km) > Jharkhand (79,716) > Himachal Pradesh (55,673) > Uttarakhand (smallest).

19-024.r: Area descending → Rajasthan (342,239 sq km) > Maharashtra (307,713) > Karnataka (191,791) > Tamil Nadu (130,060).

19-025.r: Smallest by area among UP, MP, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand → Uttarakhand (53483 sq km); Rajasthan (342239) is the largest.

19-026.r: Bihar → 3rd largest state by population (104,099,452, Census 2011) and 12th by area (94,163 sq km).

19-027.r: UP borders 8 states: Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Bihar; also Delhi (NCT) and Nepal. Not Punjab.

19-028.r: Assam → borders 7 states: West Bengal, Nagaland, Mizoram, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Tripura; countries Bangladesh and Bhutan; no UT.

19-029.r: Chhattisgarh borders UP, MP, Odisha, Jharkhand, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Telangana; not Bihar.

19-030.r: Highest altitude among the options → Bengaluru (about 920 m); Nagpur 312.41 m, Delhi 213–305 m, Jodhpur 250–300 m.

19-031.r: Rajasthan desert → world's most densely populated desert (83 persons/sq km); about 10,000 years old; only 40–60% area farmable; more net sown area cut grazing land. All true.

19-032.r: Arunachal Pradesh → on 28° N, like northern Rajasthan; about 80% forest cover (ISFR 2023: 78.67%); about 14% of forest is protected area.

19-033.r: Seven sisters → Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura; West Bengal is not one.

19-034.r: Andhra State (October 1953, carved from Madras after Potti Shriramulu's fast unto death in 1952) → capital Kurnool; Hyderabad became capital in 1956.

19-035.r: Most districts → Uttar Pradesh (75); Madhya Pradesh 55, Tamil Nadu 38, Maharashtra 36.

19-036.r: Largest district by area → Kutch, Gujarat (45,674 sq km) > Leh (45,100) > Jaisalmer (38,401) > Barmer (28,387).

19-037.r: Sonbhadra (UP; carved from Mirzapur on 4 March 1989) → touches four states: Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Bihar.

19-038.r: When asked, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka each bordered the most states. Telangana now borders Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh.

19-040.r: Wrong pair: Manipur–Aizawl; Manipur's capital is Imphal, Aizawl is Mizoram's. Correct: Tripura–Agartala; Nagaland–Kohima; Arunachal Pradesh–Itanagar.

19-042.r: Capital of Rajasthan → Jaipur, the 'Pink City'; Hawa Mahal is there.

19-044.r: 29th state → Telangana, capital Hyderabad; after J&K's reorganisation India has 28 states.

19-045.r: Correct pair: Mizoram–Aizawl. Assam → Dispur; Meghalaya → Shillong; Nagaland → Kohima.

19-046.r: Not a planned capital → Bengaluru; Chandigarh, Bhubaneswar and Gandhinagar are planned cities.

19-047.r: Assam → Dispur; Nagaland → Kohima; Arunachal Pradesh → Itanagar; Meghalaya → Shillong.

19-048.r: Assam → Dispur; Mizoram → Aizawl; Gujarat → Gandhinagar; Manipur → Imphal.

19-049.r: State touching most state boundaries → Uttar Pradesh: 8 states (Rajasthan, Haryana, Himachal, Uttarakhand, Bihar, MP, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh) and one UT (Delhi).

19-050.r: MP borders UP, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan; not Jharkhand (which borders Bihar, West Bengal, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, UP).

19-053.r: MP's longest border → with Uttar Pradesh (north); Chhattisgarh to the east, Maharashtra south, Gujarat and Rajasthan west.
